precepts.text: The sanctuary is dedicated again on the very day the heathen had profaned it, the dedication Daniel's cleansing points to.
precepts.point: The cleansing of the sanctuary goes into Hanukkah, the feast of dedication. That history is recorded in First Maccabees.

note.label: Daniel 8: The Ram and the Goat

precepts.why:
The saint asked “How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?” and the answer was “Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.” The cleansing of the sanctuary goes into Hanukkah, the feast of dedication, and that history is recorded in First Maccabees.

“Now on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and eighth year, they rose up betimes in the morning, And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made.” The daily sacrifice was offered again, according to the law, upon a new altar.

“Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals.” The sanctuary was dedicated again on the very day the heathen had profaned it. That dedication, on the twenty-fifth day of the month Casleu, is what Daniel's cleansing of the sanctuary points to.

precepts.text: The standard for the body is blameless conversation and pleasure in the law of the Most High.
precepts.point: Fear came on every soul, and all that believed were together and had all things common. Having all things common means the same speech and the same mind, perfectly joined together, with blameless conversation and pleasure in the law, so that when the mind is fixed on the law, materialistic things stop mattering.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
When the sanctuary was cleansed, Judas “chose priests of blameless conversation, such as had pleasure in the law”. That is the standard for the body: blameless conversation and pleasure in the law of the Most High.

Having all things common means the same speech and the same mind, perfectly joined together. When the mind is fixed on the law, materialistic things stop mattering, which is how all that believed could be together, sell their possessions and goods, and part them to every man as he had need.

precepts.text: Judas said the enemies, the Greeks, were discomfited, so they went up to dedicate the sanctuary.
precepts.point: The feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10 commemorates the Maccabees driving out the Greeks and rededicating the temple the Greeks had profaned. Christ would not turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“Then said Judas and his brethren, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.”

The enemies who were discomfited were the Greeks. That is the dedication of the sanctuary the feast of dedication in John 10 remembers, and it is why Christ, who kept that feast, was not accepting Greeks as his own a few months later. The Grecians of Acts 6 are Israelites, not the enemies Judas drove out.

precepts.text: The temple was rededicated on the very day the heathen had profaned it.
precepts.point: Read logically, using comparison and context. Christianity teaches people to read the bible with a slave mind, taking a verse at face value the way the slave master intended, instead of going back to the beginning as you would with any book or film.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals.”

The temple was rededicated on the very day the heathen had profaned it, and the heathen were the Greeks. That is the feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10, and it shows who the Greeks were to Israel: the profaners of the sanctuary, not brethren in the church.

note.label: Who & What is the Abomination of Desolation

precepts.why:
It says then shall the sanctuary be cleansed: “Then Judas appointed certain men to fight against those that were in the fortress, until he had cleansed the sanctuary.”

“So he chose priests of blameless conversation, such as had pleasure in the law”. See the warriors he chose. He couldn’t get just anybody to go do this thing; he said I need priests of blameless conversation who have pleasure in the law. That’s the type of brothers I like around me: brothers of blameless conversation that got pleasure in the law. When brothers come around we’ll be talking about scriptures, and then brothers be on that phone looking for stats of football players. Get the hell away from me, go over there and sit down somewhere; you ain’t ready for this, little boy. Sitting around thinking about some woman with a big behind, go sit down somewhere. I need men around me who love the law of the Most High. Those are the warriors; that’s who God is dealing with. The rest of you with your comic books, he ain’t dealing with you yet.

A sister wrote, make me believe I’m the only woman on the earth to you. Kick her to the curb: that’s a broken spirit, she ain’t ready for marriage. She wants to be an idol to him. Brother, you better find you a revolutionary woman who understands the Bible, who says you better go out there and fight for our people, fight for the laws of God. Any other kind of woman, don’t waste your time on her; she ain’t ready for this. And be careful, because some sisters lie till you get married: I’ll be the revolution and I’ll be exactly what you want until I get you.

note.label: Who & What is the Abomination of Desolation

precepts.why:
Back to First Maccabees 4:41 again: we want to find out who the real soldiers are. Priests of blameless conversation such as had pleasure in the law: those are the soldiers, the warriors the Lord is looking for. I hope y’all men understand that. “Who cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.”

“The altar of burnt offerings, which was profaned”: it was profaned because they sacrificed swine, pig, on the altar, and they put up the idol of Jupiter Olympus. “They thought it best to pull it down, lest it should be a reproach to them, because the heathen had defiled it”, “And laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.” There were no prophets at that time: the intertestamental period, as the scholars call it, the time when there were no prophets.

“Then they took whole stones according to the law”: and as great as Judah Maccabee was, he never said I have a hundred percent truth. Be mindful of men that say they know everything; head for the hills when you hear men speak like that. They can’t even get out of the ghetto, but they know everything. “And built a new altar according to the former”: in order to build a new altar you had to know the law; you had to know the height and width of the altar. “And made up the sanctuary, and the things that were within the temple, and hallowed the courts.”

“They made also new holy vessels, and into the temple they brought the candlestick”: the candlestick is the seven-branch menorah, like the two we have up here, and all of them should be lit. Our custom is never to light one each day; we light the whole thing at once. “And upon the altar they burned incense, and the lamps that were upon the candlestick they lighted, that they might give light in the temple.” The lamps that were upon the candlestick: that’s all seven. They lit all seven; they didn’t light one one day and one the next day. “Furthermore they set the loaves upon the table, and spread out the veils, and finished all the works which they had begun to make.”

“Now on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and eighth year”: the five and twentieth day is the 25th, and Casleu is the ninth month, which we call today November; when you start at March you got March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November. “They rose up betimes in the morning, And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made.”

“Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals.” The same day that they defiled the temple was the same date, years later, that we dedicated it: the 25th of the ninth month. With songs and citherns and harps and cymbals we rejoiced; we partied.

“Then all the people fell upon their faces, worshipping and praising the God of heaven, who had given them good success.” I always pray for the good success of the nation of Israel. We want good success, so we got to pray to God Almighty, whose name is Yahuwah. You must pray.

“And so they kept the dedication of the altar eight days”: eight days, not seven days, eight days, “and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and sacrificed the sacrifice of deliverance and praise.”

“It was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.” In November it gets cold. Christ kept the feast of dedication in the winter, and walked in the temple because it was a holy convocation.

Then king Herod added to the temple they had built, from 19 BC to 63 AD, continually building to make it more elaborate and fancy.

points: Chapter 4 is the cleansing of the temple and the rededicating of the altar. “He chose priests of blameless conversation, such as had pleasure in the law”. That is who your circle has to be. If you want things to get better, change your circle. Fringes and a border of blue don’t make everybody right. Coming in, a man can keep getting in trouble because his circle is idiots: fights on 42nd Street with some clowns, jumping the turnstile and getting arrested. Look around and see it: these are a bunch of idiots, and I am an idiot for being with these clowns. Change your circle, and go be around the elders.

They cleansed the sanctuary and bare out the defiled stones. The altar of burnt offerings the heathen had defiled they pulled down, and laid up the stones “until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.” They said, we must wait for a prophet to show us what to do.

They built a new altar of whole stones according to the law, made new holy vessels, and “into the temple they brought the candlestick”: that is the menorah. They lighted the lamps “that they might give light in the temple”, set the loaves on the table and spread out the veils.

“On the five and twentieth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Casleu”: the ninth month is November. They offered sacrifice according to the law on the new altar. That is the feast of dedication.
“They kept the dedication of the altar eight days and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and sacrificed the sacrifice of deliverance and praise.”
